request: What did CRS report about Medicare prescription drug price negotiation and its expected savings?

reply.reply:
**CRS reported CBO estimates that Medicare drug price negotiation would reduce the deficit by $25 billion, with 2031 drug prices 8% lower in Part D and 9% lower in Part B.**

- CRS reported CBO estimates that negotiation would reduce the deficit by $25 billion and lower Part D and Part B drug prices in 2031 by 8% and 9%, respectively. (R47555, PDF p. 4)
- CRS said savings from the program were expected to help fund other IRA provisions, including a $2,000 annual out-of-pocket cap beginning in 2025. (R47555, PDF p. 4)
reply.reasoning: The CRS implementation report states the CBO deficit estimate and projected Part D and Part B price reductions. It also says the savings were expected to help fund other IRA provisions, including the annual out-of-pocket cap.
